title: SKU micro-profiles and adaptive version-locking for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: produce lightweight per-SKU micro-profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) that capture latency distributions across sequence-length buckets and transient load states, and wire those artifacts into an automatic 'adaptive version-locking' flow used by the onboarding pipeline and the runtime routing decision engine. The goal is to reduce unexpected serving regressions when new model package versions are introduced and to provide targeted rollback/lock recommendations by SKU rather than coarse global pins.

Why: Current onboarding publishes broad hardware signatures that signal stability but miss short-term drift modes (thermal throttling, NVLink saturation, driver patch differences) which can cause p95 regressions for specific SKUs. By building micro-profiles and an adaptive locking signal, we can surface SKU-level instability earlier and automate conservative serving decisions without manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-profile schema established and stored in artifact registry for A100/H100/L40S/MI300
Daily job emits micro-profile diffs and a stability score per (model_version, SKU, seq_bucket)
Onboarding pipeline consumes stability score and produces an adaptive-lock recommendation: allow, soft-lock, or require-manual-review
Runtime uses adaptive-lock recommendations to prefer stable variants and exposes per-request routing reason in traces
Docs and console UI surfaces SKU stability score and the last 7 days of micro-profile diffs
work_log: 2025-02-10 Kickoff: aligned scope with product and runtime teams. Agreed to focus on sequence buckets [1-64,65-256,257-1024] and ambient load states (idle, normal, high).
2025-02-14 Data schema draft posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/SKU+Microprofile+Schema
2025-02-18 Small-scale collector implemented for A100 and L40S in perf-lab; collects 1k requests per seq-bucket to validate histograms (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/448)
2025-02-22 Initial EWMA-based stability score prototype validated against historical runs; detected 2 out of 3 injected regressions in replay tests
2025-02-26 Integration spike with onboarding pipeline: produced first adaptive-lock recommendation for sample model (v1.3.2) on H100
2025-03-01 Design review with Console PM: agreed to show 'SKU stability' as a per-model card and include link to micro-profile diff graph
decisions: Use compressed histogram format (DDSketch) for micro-profile storage to balance fidelity and registry size
Stability score = weighted combination of p95 drift, tail mass increase, and failure-rate delta; thresholds: <0.2 stable, 0.2-0.5 soft-lock, >0.5 require-manual-review
Adaptive-locking categories will be exposed to the runtime as three-level policy rather than booleans to allow gradual degradation strategies
Sequence-length buckets chosen to match existing runtime optimizations and to minimize telemetry cardinality
test_plan: Unit tests for micro-profile serializer/deserializer (roundtrip fidelity > 99% for p95)
Replay tests: inject synthetic tail latency regressions and verify stability score escalation and adaptive-lock result
End-to-end canary: publish micro-profiles for a test model across all SKUs and validate console UI rendering and runtime adoption
Load test: ensure daily micro-profile job completes within 30 minutes for fleet of 5k model-variant-SKU combinations
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (canary): enable collection and score emission for 10 models in perf-lab; runtime treats adaptive recommendations as advisory (no automatic locking)
Phase 2 (opt-in): onboarding pipeline writes recommendations to model metadata and console surfaces 'soft-lock' flags; select customers invited to opt-in
Phase 3 (enforced): runtime honors soft-lock for low-tier variants and automatically routes to fallback variants when score>0.5 for >12h
Rollback plan: if false positives observed, backfill previous 7-day profiles and revert to advisory-only mode while thresholds are tuned
